([[Dumont, New Jersey]]) * [[St. Joseph's Prep|St. Joseph's Prep]]
([[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]) }} | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = [[Overtime Elite|Team Overtime]] | years2 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team2 = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | years3 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = →[[Austin Spurs]] | years4 = {{nbay|2024|full=y}} | team4 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | years5 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team5 = →[[College Park Skyhawks]] | years6 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team6 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | highlights = * [[NBA G League]] Next Up Game ([[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]]) }} '''Dominick Barlow''' (born May 26, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). ==High school career== As a freshman for [[St. Joseph’s Prep]], Barlow saw his season cut short due to a torn labrum in his shoulder. Upon going into his sophomore year, he transferred to Dumont High School closer to his native North Jersey. Barlow attended [[Dumont High School]] in his hometown of [[Dumont, New Jersey]].Toussaint, Jensen. [https://philadelphia.today/2024/01/dominick-barlow-basketball-nba/ "Former St. Joseph’s Prep Basketball Player Soaks Up Opportunity To Play in the NBA"], ''Philadelphia Today'', January 28, 2024. Accessed July 19, 2025. "As a freshman for St. Joseph’s Prep, Barlow saw his season cut short due to a torn labrum in his shoulder. Upon going into his sophomore year, he transferred to Dumont High School closer to his native North Jersey." Barlow assumed a leading role in his junior season and averaged 23.3 points and 12.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Polacheck |first1=Jacob |title=Dominick Barlow is Storming His Way onto NBA Draft Boards with a Rather Unique Pathway |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2022/02/24/dominick-barlow-is-storming-his-way-onto-nba-draft-boards-with-a-rather-unique-pathway/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=June 18, 2022 |date=February 24, 2022}} During his senior season, which was limited to eight games by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], he averaged 27.6 points, 17 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 2.6 blocks per game. Barlow was named North Jersey Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Mattura |first1=Greg |title=North Jersey basketball star, just a few months out of HS, signs million-dollar deal |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2021/09/14/dominick-barlow-former-nj-basketball-star-signs-million-dollar-deal/8324058002/ |work=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]] |access-date=June 17, 2022 |date=September 14, 2021}} He played for the New York Rens at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]], helping the team reach the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League#Peach Jam|Peach Jam]] semifinals.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=NBA Draft Combine: 18-year-old N.J. native Dominick Barlow could hear his named called at the NBA Draft after pursuing unique path |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2022/05/nba-draft-combine-18-year-old-nj-native-dominick-barlow-could-hear-his-named-called-at-the-nba-draft-after-pursuing-unique-path.html |publisher=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=June 17, 2022 |date=May 22, 2022}} Barlow was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and intended to play a [[Postgraduate year|postgraduate]] season at [[Bridgton Academy]] in [[Bridgton, Maine]] before pursuing professional options. ==Professional career== ===Team Overtime (2021–2022)=== On September 2, 2021, Barlow signed with Team Overtime for the [[Overtime Elite]]'s inaugural season.{{cite web |title=Overtime Elite Signs Skilled Forward Dominick Barlow |url=https://overtime.app.box.com/s/eac033xfxcpbbmhq40g0qptzrvpyx67k |publisher=Overtime Elite |access-date=June 17, 2022 |date=September 2, 2021}} He played for Team Overtime in OTE, averaging 14.8 points and 5.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Graham |first1=Pat |title=New league for prep standouts sends 2 players to NBA Draft combine |url=https://www.nba.com/news/new-league-for-prep-standouts-sends-2-players-to-nba-draft-combine |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=June 17, 2022 |date=May 19, 2022}} ===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2022–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Barlow signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], becoming the first [[Overtime Elite]] player to make an NBA roster.{{cite web|author=saslpederson|title=SPURS SIGN DOMINICK BARLOW TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-dominick-barlow-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2022|access-date=July 13, 2022}} Barlow joined the Spurs' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster and made his Summer League debut on July 8, 2022, scoring nine points and seven rebounds in a 90–99 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612759/spurs|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 13, 2022}}{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs vs Cleveland Cavaliers Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/sas-vs-cle-1522200004/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 13, 2022}} Barlow made his proper NBA debut with the Spurs on November 2, 2022, by getting two points and three assists in a 143–100 blowout loss against the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|title=Toronto Raptors at San Antonio Spurs Box Score, November 2, 2022|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202211020SAS.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2024}} On January 28, 2023, in 126–110 loss to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] in the [[NBA G League]], Barlow finished with a double-double career-high game of 32 points, 10 rebounds, and 3 blocks for Austin.{{cite web|title=Spurs' Dominick Barlow: Posts double-double|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-dominick-barlow-posts-double-double-416017/|website=CBSSports.com|date=January 29, 2023|access-date=February 13, 2023}}{{cite web|title=Spurs vs. Vipers – NBA G League Box Score – January 28, 2023|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-g-league/boxscore/_/gameId/401481942|website=ESPN.com|access-date=February 13, 2023}} On April 2, 2023, Barlow recorded his first double-double in the NBA with 12 points and 10 rebounds alongside a season-high 5 assists in a 142–134 overtime win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs at Sacramento Kings Box Score, April 2, 2023|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202304020SAC.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2024}} In the final game of Barlow's rookie season just a week later, he recorded career-highs of 21 points and 19 rebounds in a 138–117 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs at Dallas Mavericks Box Score, April 9, 2023|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202304090DAL.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2024}} On July 27, 2023, Barlow signed a two-way contract for the [[2023–24 NBA season]].{{cite web|title=Spurs Re-Sign Dominick Barlow to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-re-sign-dominick-barlow-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2023|access-date=July 27, 2023}} He was converted to a standard NBA contract on March 2, 2024.{{cite tweet|first=Tom|last=Orsborn|title=#Spurs make the following moves reported earlier official: 1, They've converted Barlow’s two-way deal to a standard NBA contract; 2, They've signed RaiQuan Gray and Jamaree Bouyea to two-way deals; 3, They've waived forward Mamadi Diakite.|number=1764032846534959265|user=tom_orsborn|date=March 2, 2024|access-date=March 2, 2024}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2024–2025)=== On July 30, 2024, Barlow signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Forward Dominick Barlow to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-forward-dominick-barlow-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2024|access-date=July 30, 2024}} On March 4, 2025, Barlow signed a standard two-year contract with the Hawks.{{cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Announce They Have Signed Dominick Barlow To New Multi-Year Contract |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-announce-they-have-signed-dominick-barlow-to-new-multi-year-contract-01jnheat5fgd |website=SI |publisher=SI.com}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2025–present)=== On July 9, 2025, Barlow signed a two-way contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web | last1=Miller | first1=Will | last2=De Siver | first2=Hunter | title=Report: Philadelphia 76ers Waiving Former Alabama Player Alex Reese | website=Alabama Crimson Tide On SI | date=2025-07-09 | url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/basketball/report-philadelphia-76ers-waiving-former-alabama-player-alex-reese | access-date=2025-12-06}} On February 2, 2026, in a game against the [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]], Barlow recorded a career-high 26 points, along with 16 rebounds, including 10 offensive.{{Cite web |last=Levick • • |first=Noah |date=2026-02-03 |title=Observations after brilliant Barlow's career-high night helps Sixers top Clippers |url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/sixers-vs-clippers-dominick-barlow-career-high-tyrese-maxey-joel-embiid/711067/ |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=NBC Sports Philadelphia |language=en-US}} On February 5, he signed a standard NBA contract of 2-years, $6.8 million with the 76ers.{{Cite web |date=2026-02-06 |title=Report: Sixers Signing Key Rotation Player to Standard NBA Contract |url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/onsi/report-sixers-signing-key-rotation-player-to-standard-nba-contract-01kgr1z67ahd |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=Philadelphia 76ers On SI |language=en-US}} Barlow made 71 appearances (including 59 starts) for Philadelphia during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 7.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 1.2 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dominick Barlow 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4870562/dominick-barlow|access-date=June 12, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics==
